name: Aurora Phenomena (Northern and Southern Lights Folklore)
description: Aurora phenomena — the Aurora Borealis (Northern Lights) and Aurora Australis (Southern Lights) — are natural light displays in Earth's upper atmosphere caused by charged solar particles interacting with the magnetosphere, and have inspired rich and varied supernatural traditions across polar and sub-polar cultures worldwide.

aliases.name: Aurora Borealis
aliases.meaning: Northern dawn — from Aurora (Roman goddess of dawn) and Boreas (Greek north wind)

aliases.name: Aurora Australis
aliases.meaning: Southern dawn — from Aurora and Auster (Latin south wind)

aliases.name: Guovssahas
aliases.meaning: The light you can hear — reflects Sami belief that the aurora makes a rustling sound

aliases.name: Revontulet
aliases.meaning: Fox fires — from the legend of a cosmic fox running across the sky, its tail brushing sparks

aliases.name: Bifrost
aliases.meaning: Trembling or shimmering road — the bridge connecting the world of the living to Asgard (sometimes identified with the aurora in Norse tradition)

origin: Aurora borealis occurs in a ring around the Arctic (auroral oval), centered on the geomagnetic pole. During strong geomagnetic storms it can be seen as far south as the northern United States, central Europe, and occasionally further. Aurora australis similarly occurs around the Antarctic. Both appear year-round but require darkness and clear skies to be visible.
